look_here_first: Start with texture and leaf arrangement. Roughstem rosinweed is a perennial with very rough, sandpapery leaves and stems, broad sessile leaves, and yellow sunflower-like heads. Use the coarse scabrous surface plus stem-leaf arrangement and peduncle length to separate it from nearby Silphium concepts.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: perennial herb; several stems from base; stems and leaves conspicuously rough/scabrous; broad sessile leaves; leaves may be opposite below and alternate above; yellow radiate heads; heads relatively close to leafy upper stems compared with longer-peduncled relatives; foliage aromatic/resinous when crushed

key_traits.label: Comparison training
key_traits.text: Compared with S. laciniatum, leaves are broad rather than deeply pinnatifid. Compared with S. integrifolium sensu stricto, S. radula is typically rougher/hairier and may show mixed opposite/alternate leaf arrangement.
